source_boundary: The handler calls prepare_workspace_policy before scheduler/native worker admission. Its None result plus no emergency-safe bypass yields native_policy_not_ready.
The owned publishing worker registers the workspace, starts idempotently, reads the existing last_error, and waits only if the last_error is not a nonempty string.

On macOS/Linux this readiness cap is 2.0 seconds, bounded further by the original incoming HTTP deadline. Windows uses 8.0 seconds. The separate workspace lifecycle 400 ms contract is not this hook readiness cap.
Both current_snapshot_binding and fallback current_snapshot are tried; each can mark expiry and refuse unacked/closed/absent authority. The owned publishing worker then returns None.
A successful wait does not guarantee authority remains available for the subsequent getters; any later withdrawal stays a real failed admission.

Original stop_resident contains the native owner then closes worker client streams. It does not explicitly notify the publisher; the original polling/generation path independently detects replacement and requests publication.
